      "content": "30|
31|A strange visitor once met with the local Flamekeeper to discuss divine grace and spent time with the wax elemental in secret. The visitor infused it with an energy called a **mote of the divine**, then left after declaring the result “yet another failed experiment.” The infusion awakened the elemental and gave it the power to absorb other creatures.
32|
33|## Adventure Summary
34|
35|- **Monster:** The Pontiff, an egomaniacal wax elemental disguised as a respected Flamekeeper.
36|- **Motivation:** Enlighten the congregation by melting and absorbing their bodies.
37|- **Previous actions:** Weekly festivals select pilgrims for “transcendence”; those pilgrims disappear.
38|- **Location:** The Pontiff holds private services in a major chapel of [[The Faith of the Sacred Flame]] on [[Nevercough Island]].
39|
40|## Stickyickistan Connections
41|
42|- **[[The Faith of the Sacred Flame]]:** The chapel follows the dominant faith of [[Mythmos]], including the tenets of the Hearth, Lantern, Torch, and Candle. The Pontiff has twisted the Candle’s promise of hope and redemption into literal “enlightenment.”
43|- **[[Nevercough Island]]:** The chapel sits among the island’s ruling institutions, wealthy districts, and political interests. A scandal involving missing pilgrims will attract attention from officials, clergy, journalists, and opportunists.
44|- **[[The Rolling Papers]]:** The public investigation may begin with a missing-person notice, a report about the strange feast, or a formal request from the chapel. The paper’s coverage can determine whether the congregation is treated as victims or suspects.
45|- **[[FLS Guildhall]]:** The Free League can register the party, provide basic research, and record the consequences of the chapel’s collapse. The Guildhall is not responsible for protecting the clergy’s reputation.
46|- **[[The Loot Tavern]]:** [[Cacophonics]]’s connection to the chapel gives the party an existing musician who can identify the organ’s importance and help expose the Pontiff’s fear of thunderous sound.
47|- **[[Dr. Stein]]:** If the adventure follows the Motes of the Divine thread, the Pontiff’s divine infusion can be treated as another dangerous experiment related to the biomantic and Magitech research surrounding Stein, without making him the sole creator.
48|
49|## Adventure Hooks
50|
51|### Curiosity: The Final Feast
52|
53|A public notice in [[The Rolling Papers]] announces a special Sacred Flame feast on [[Nevercough Island]]. A traveling Flamekeeper carrying candles and supplies urges the characters to attend the celebration and witness the supposed divine revelation.
54|
55|### Morality: Those Left Behind
56|
57|Notices of missing pilgrims crowd a board near the [[FLS Guildhall]]. A distraught spouse explains that their partner attended a Sacred Flame feast, was selected for a “special ceremony,” and never returned. The spouse asks the characters to investigate before the authorities dismiss the disappearance as voluntary pilgrimage.
58|
59|### Compensation: Fuel for the Fire
60|
61|A battered Flamekeeper arrives at the [[FLS Guildhall]] after a supply wagon carrying replacement candles for the island chapel was attacked on the road. The Flamekeeper escaped with one crate, but the driver and the rest of the shipment are missing. With the chapel’s stores running low before the upcoming feast, they offer the relief funds they have left for protection while the characters deliver the surviving candles and investigate what happened to the rest of the convoy.
62|
63|## Local Flamekeeper
64|
65|The local Flamekeeper is a lawful good human cleric who serves as the party’s initial contact. They are earnest, overworked, and deeply concerned that the chapel’s leadership has changed without explanation.
66|
67|**Personality:** Fidgety, optimistic, and eager to help.  
68|**Desire:** Protect the congregation and expose the truth without abandoning the people who still need the faith.  
69|**Fear:** Losing the community’s trust or discovering that the Sacred Flame has been used to justify the disappearances.
70|
71|> “Are you okay? Is there anything you need? How can I be of service?”
72|
73|The Flamekeeper knows that:
74|
75|- Weekly feasts are held for the supposed Pontiff at the island chapel.
76|- They have been away from the chapel for several weeks on relief work.
77|- The previous Flamekeeper was respected and apparently received a miraculous vision.
78|- Senior clergy claim the congregation has entered a new age of enlightenment.
79|- The official story is that selected pilgrims leave the island blessed, but the missing-person notices say otherwise.
80|

88|
